## Why a config file instead of a wrapper

Every other integration in this repo works because its agent exposes lifecycle hooks. Aider exposes none — just `--notifications-command`, and `hooks.go:22-39` documents how weak that is: no argv, no environment, no stdin, output discarded, and it only fires when `notifications: true` is *also* set (`io.py:1090` guards on `bell_on_next_input and notifications`).

The obvious fallback is a wrapper — ship an `entire-aider` command that shells out to aider with the flags baked in. Two things kill that:

1. **Capture becomes opt-in per invocation.** The user has to remember to type the wrapper. Any plain `aider` run in the repo is invisible — and that's the run they'll actually make when they're in a hurry, which is exactly when they want a checkpoint.
2. **`install-hooks`/`uninstall-hooks` stop meaning anything.** The protocol wants installation to be a real, inspectable, reversible state. A wrapper has no install step to perform and nothing to uninstall.

The config file gets both. Aider loads `.aider.conf.yml` from the git root via configargparse (`main.py:474-475`), so writing a managed block there means a bare `aider` is captured with no new habit. And the block is delimited by markers (`hooks.go:17-20`), so `replaceManagedBlock` can add, update, or remove it while preserving the user's own settings byte-for-byte — `TestInstallHooks_PreservesUserConfig` asserts uninstall restores the original file exactly, and `TestUninstallHooks_RemovesOwnFile` asserts the file disappears if it only ever held our block.

Two details in that block are load-bearing, and both have tests guarding them: `notifications: true` (without it the command is a silent no-op), and the `echo {}` prefix — Entire's bridge rejects an empty stdin read *before* the plugin runs, and aider surfaces any non-zero exit as `Failed to run notifications command: ...` on every turn.

## Why a fingerprint instead of a turn index

Because the bell isn't a turn-end signal. `ring_bell` is reached from `get_input()`, `confirm_ask()` *and* `prompt_ask()`, so it fires at whatever interactive prompt comes first after `llm_started()` — and the ordering inside `Coder.send_message` is what makes a turn index wrong:

```
1423  llm_started()        → arms the bell
1531  show_usage_report()  → "> Tokens: ..."
1585  apply_updates()      → "> Applied edit to ..."
1589  auto_commit()        → git commit
```

A turn needing no confirmation rings once, cleanly, after everything. A turn with a confirmation prompt inside `apply_updates` rings *mid-turn* — after the usage report, before the commit — and then rings again later. Same turn index, twice. Worse, a lint/test reflection loop makes several API calls within one turn.

So an index can only produce one of two failure modes: dedup on it and you drop real work that happened in the same turn after the first firing; don't dedup and you checkpoint the same state repeatedly, which for aider is the normal case rather than an edge case.

`{turn index, usage-report count, applied-edit count}` measures *observable progress* instead of position. `advancedOver` (`state.go:36-41`) accepts a higher turn index, or — at the same index — more reports or more edits. A second firing that sees nothing new is dropped; one that sees another API round or another landed edit is real. `TestParseHook_TurnEndFiresAgainOnMoreEditsInSameTurn` is the case an index can't express.

The zero-work guard in `parseTurnEnd` (`hooks.go:250`) is the other half: a bell rung at "Add foo.go to the chat?" before any model response has neither a report nor an edit, so it produces nothing at all.

## Two commits

- `24a9739` — the four test files, the `loadState` null fix, and BUILDATHON.md. The fix matters for the same reason as above: a state file containing literal `null` unmarshalled into a zeroed struct reporting `TurnIndex == 0`, which the dedup logic reads as "turn 0 already checkpointed" and swallows the session's first turn. Unmarshalling through a pointer catches it; `TestLoadState_CorruptFileIsNotFatal` covers `null` alongside the other corruption shapes.
- `f4cc359` — the config churn that was also in the tree: Claude Code hook matchers renamed to `Agent`/`TaskCreate|TaskUpdate`, `SubagentStop` added, every hook guarded on `entire` being on PATH, plus the entire-graph pointer blocks and the telemetry/gitignore changes. Separated because it's unrelated to the aider adapter.

One thing worth flagging rather than fixing: `.entire/settings.json` now has `telemetry: false` committed for everyone on the repo, not just you. If that was a local preference it belongs in `.entire/settings.local.json` instead.

## Part 1 — Prior work, reconstructed from Entire checkpoints (no code read)

Four checkpoints on `main`, two sessions, all from today:

| Checkpoint | Commit | What it was |
|---|---|---|
| `e42c966daba2` | `24a9739` | Test coverage for the aider adapter + the `loadState` null fix |
| `65db6b1a974f` | `f4cc359` | Repo config refresh (Claude Code hook matchers, entire-graph pointers) |
| `c47c0664af62` | `8327df7` | BUILDATHON.md — semantic-diff findings |
| `cdaa07c8-f2d` | `2c168d6` | "push it" (temporary) |

**What I built:** `entire-agent-aider`, an external agent adapter. Aider exposes no lifecycle hooks at all — only `--notifications-command`, which gets no argv, no environment, no stdin, discards output, and only fires when `notifications: true` is also set.

**Architecture, and why:**

1. **Config-file installation, not a wrapper.** A managed marker-delimited block in `.aider.conf.yml` at the git root (aider loads it via configargparse). A wrapper was rejected on two grounds: capture becomes opt-in per invocation (a bare `aider` run — the one you make when you're in a hurry — goes uncaptured), and `install-hooks`/`uninstall-hooks` stop meaning anything. Two load-bearing details in the block, each test-guarded: `notifications: true`, and the `echo {}` prefix (Entire's bridge rejects empty stdin before the plugin runs; a non-zero exit surfaces as a per-turn error banner in aider).

2. **Fingerprint dedup, not a turn index.** The bell is not a turn-end signal — `ring_bell` is reachable from `get_input()`, `confirm_ask()` and `prompt_ask()`, so it can fire mid-turn (after the usage report, before the commit) and again later at the same turn index; a lint/test reflection loop makes several API calls inside one turn. The fingerprint `{turn index, usage-report count, applied-edit count}` measures observable progress instead of position; `advancedOver` accepts a higher index, or more reports/edits at the same index. Plus a zero-work guard in `parseTurnEnd` so a bell rung at "Add foo.go to the chat?" produces nothing.

3. **State durability.** `loadState` unmarshals through a pointer — a state file containing literal `null` previously zeroed into `TurnIndex == 0`, which dedup read as "turn 0 already checkpointed" and swallowed the session's first turn.

**Verified state at last commit:** `go test ./...` green, 65 cases, 92.1% statement coverage. The semantic diff over `f31731c..HEAD` proved exactly one changed production entity (`loadState`, 5 dependents) against 45 added test functions.

**Open risk carried forward:** `.entire/settings.json` has `telemetry: false` committed repo-wide; that belongs in `settings.local.json` if it was a local preference.

---

## Part 2 — Graph findings

### `entire graph impact --symbol parseTurns --depth 2`

`parseTurns` — `agents/entire-agent-aider/internal/aider/transcript.go:55` (span 55–90).
Blast radius: **12 callers** (8 direct, 4 transitive), 5 callees, 2 type consumers, 3 data flows.

**Direct callers (4 production, 4 test):**
- `Agent.ReadSession` — `agent.go:178` (def `:147`) — session/summary read path
- `Agent.parseTurnEnd` — `hooks.go:239` (def `:233`) — **checkpoint-writing path**
- `readTurns` — `transcript.go:195` (def `:187`) — shared reader
- `Agent.CalculateTokens` — `transcript.go:261`
- `TestFingerprintOf`, `TestParseTurns_Fixture`, `TestParseTurns_BlankPromptIsEmpty`, `TestParseTurns_LineEndingAgnostic`

**Transitive (via the two hubs above):**
- `Agent.ParseHook` — `hooks.go:187` *(via `parseTurnEnd`)*
- `Agent.GetTranscriptPosition` — `transcript.go:205`, `Agent.ExtractModifiedFiles` — `:215`, `Agent.ExtractPrompts` — `:235` *(all via `readTurns`)*

**Callees (5) — all Markdown-shape-specific:** `splitLines:19`, `isPromptLine:32`, `promptLineText:37`, `blockquoteText:45`, `absorbToolLine:92`.

**Type consumers:** `turn` (`types.go:94`) as both `RETURNS_TYPE` and `USES_TYPE` — and nothing else.

**Co-change / siblings:** none. `transcript.go` has no historical coupling to other files.

### `entire graph search --query "transcript parsing and lifecycle event handling"`

Top aider hits: `parseTurnEnd` (`hooks.go:233–277`), `parseTurns` (`transcript.go:55`), `ParseHook` (`hooks.go:184–195`), `transcriptPath` (`agent.go:122`), plus related `sessionEvent` (`hooks.go:198`) and `ResolveSessionFile` (`agent.go:114`).

Cross-agent, the default-profile run surfaced **kiro** as the in-repo precedent for two-format support: `parseTranscript` (`kiro/transcript.go:774`) dispatches `isCLITranscript` → else `tryParseIDETranscript`.

---

## The affected surface, grouped

**Parsers** — `parseTurns` + its 5 Markdown-specific callees; `readTurns` as the shared file→turns reader.
**Lifecycle handlers** — `ParseHook` (`hooks.go:184`) switch over `HookNameTurnEnd`/`SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`; `sessionEvent` (`hooks.go:198`); `parseTurnEnd` (`hooks.go:233`).
**Summary/read paths** — `ReadSession`, `ExtractPrompts`, `ExtractModifiedFiles`, `GetTranscriptPosition`, `CalculateTokens`.
**Checkpoint-writing path** — `parseTurnEnd` → `fingerprintOf` → `loadState`/`saveState` (`state.go`) → `protocol.EventJSON{Type: eventTurnEnd, ...}`.
**Path resolution** — `transcriptPath` (`agent.go:122`) joins a single fixed `transcriptRel`; `ResolveSessionFile` (`agent.go:114`).
**Fixtures** — only `testdata/chat_history.md` and `testdata/llm_history.log` exist; no JSONL fixture.

## Four risks the graph makes visible

1. **The format assumption lives in the callees, not the callers.** All 12 callers consume `[]turn` and nothing else — `turn` is the single type boundary. That's the good news: a format seam at or just below `parseTurns` reaches every consumer with zero caller changes, which is what satisfies "no duplicated implementation." Duplicating at the caller level would mean touching all four production callers plus three transitive ones.

Read the format and the five implementation files. Here's the mapping and where it breaks.

## What the JSONL actually gives us

Ten event types, one line each, plus a trailing blank line (line 18) that must be skipped rather than treated as an error.

| Event | Maps to | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `session_started` | **session ID, directly** | `session_id: "btw-track3-demo-001"` |
| `user_prompt` | `turn{Index, Prompt}` — opens a turn | one event = one turn, no run-collapsing needed |
| `file_changed` | `turn.ModifiedFiles` | equivalent of `Applied edit to ` |
| `usage` | `turn.Usage` | `input_tokens: 8421`, `output_tokens: 2194` — **exact integers** |
| `checkpoint_created` | **`ExtractSummary`** | `summary`, `intent`, `open_questions` |
| `session_ended` | real session-end event | `status`, `duration_seconds` |
| `agent_response`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `file_read` | nothing in `turn` | ignored, must not error |

Parsed through the existing model this file yields exactly one turn: `Prompt` = the coupon text, `ModifiedFiles` = `[src/checkout/apply_coupon.ts, tests/checkout/apply_coupon.test.ts]`, `Usage{Sent: 8421, Received: 2194, Reports: 1}` → fingerprint `{TurnIndex: 0, ReportCount: 1, EditCount: 2}`. Against `loadState`'s `{-1, 0, 0}` default, `advancedOver` returns true. **The dedup design survives the format change intact** — the fingerprint measures observable progress, and JSONL supplies all three components more directly than Markdown did.

## Three risks from my earlier report, resolved by the format

1. **`sessionIDFromBanner` returning `""` kills the checkpoint** (`hooks.go:260-263`) — gone. `session_started.session_id` is explicit. One caveat: the banner path normalizes to digits-and-dashes because Entire rejects colons in a path component. `btw-track3-demo-001` is safe, but an arbitrary `session_id` isn't, so it needs sanitizing rather than trusting.
2. **The zero-work guard is Markdown-derived** — resolved. `usage` and `file_changed` feed `ReportCount`/`EditCount` directly.
3. **Token counts are lossy above 999** (`parseTokenCount`, `transcript.go:145`) — JSONL is exact. `CalculateTokens` computes `Sent - CacheWrite - CacheHit`; with no cache fields present that yields `8421` correctly, and the negative-clamp becomes dead weight on this path rather than a bug.

**1. `ChunkTranscript` corrupts JSONL — and `parseTurns`' impact graph did not surface it.** `turnSegments` (`transcript.go:353`) calls `isPromptLine`, so it's Markdown-coupled, but it reaches those helpers as a sibling of `parseTurns`, not through it. 5	An Entire integration for [Aider](https://aider.chat) — the one widely-used AI

8	## Problem, intended user and why it matters
9	
10	**The user:** a developer who uses aider as their daily coding agent and wants
11	the same session history, checkpoints and rewind that Entire already gives
12	Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode and Pi users.
13	
14	**The problem:** aider users got none of it. Every aider session was invisible
15	to Entire — no transcript, no checkpoints, no way to recover from a bad run, no
16	record of why code changed.
17	
18	**Why it was still missing:** every other integration in this repo works because
19	its agent offers lifecycle hooks. Aider offers none. It exposes exactly one
20	outbound callback, `--notifications-command`, and reading its implementation
21	(`aider/io.py:1088`) shows five constraints that make it much weaker than it
22	looks:
23	
24	1. It only runs if `notifications: true` is *also* set — the guard is
25	   `if self.bell_on_next_input and self.notifications`. Setting just the command
26	   is a silent no-op that captures nothing.
27	2. It receives **no arguments, no environment and no stdin**, so it cannot say
28	   which session fired.
29	3. Its output is discarded (`capture_output=True`).
30	4. A non-zero exit is shown to the user as
31	   `Failed to run notifications command: ...` — a failing hook nags them on
32	   every turn.
33	5. **It is not a turn-end signal.** `ring_bell()` is reached from `get_input()`,
34	   `confirm_ask()` and `prompt_ask()`, so it fires mid-turn at any confirmation
35	   prompt, and never at all in headless mode.
36	
37	Aider also writes its own state *into the working tree* — `.aider.chat.history.md`
38	and a repo-map cache land in the repository root — where every other agent uses

## Noon Curveball: what changed and how we adapted

**The curveball.** Aider released a new JSONL transcript and lifecycle event
format. Existing users still produce the original Markdown. Three requirements:
support both without duplicating the implementation, never crash on an unknown
event, and turn an incomplete transcript into a *partial* result rather than a
discarded session.

**Where the graph pointed the change.** The same
`entire graph impact --symbol parseTurns --depth 2` from section 2 is what made
the design obvious rather than guessed:

> Type consumers (0 in, 2 out): `-> turn` [RETURNS_TYPE], `-> turn` [USES_TYPE]

All 12 callers consume `[]turn` and **nothing else**. So the format seam belongs
*below* `parseTurns`, not above it: one dispatch point reaches every caller, and
no caller changes. Putting it above would have meant editing all four production
callers plus three transitive ones and maintaining two copies of the analyzer
surface. The callee list said the same thing from the other side — `splitLines`,
`isPromptLine`, `promptLineText`, `blockquoteText`, `absorbToolLine` are all
Markdown-shape-specific, and they are exactly what a second format replaces.

The graph also **under-reported one path**, which is why its output is treated
as evidence rather than an oracle: `ChunkTranscript` never appears in
`parseTurns`' blast radius, because it reaches the Markdown helpers through
`turnSegments` as a *sibling* rather than through `parseTurns`. It was found by
reading the callee list and checking who else used those five helpers.

**What was built.**

```
                         .entire/aider/chat.md          ← path UNCHANGED
                                  │
                          detectFormat(data)            ← by CONTENT, not filename
                        ┌─────────┴─────────┐
              markdownFormat            jsonlFormat
                        └─────────┬─────────┘
                            []turn (shared)
                                  │
     fingerprint · dedup · state.json · turn-end event · the four
     transcript_analyzer methods · CalculateTokens · chunking
                          — all written ONCE
```

| Requirement | How it is met |
|---|---|
| No duplicated implementation | One IR (`turn`), two decoders behind `transcriptFormat`; everything above the interface is shared. `markdownFormat` *delegates to the original functions* — it is not a reimplementation |
| Never crash on unknown events | The JSONL decoder switches on `event` and falls through for anything else; `encoding/json` drops unknown fields for free. Mirrors the existing `ParseHook` `default: return nil, nil` one layer down |
| Partial, not discarded | Decoding is per line. A malformed line costs that one event. `parseTurns` returns **no error** — a signature that is load-bearing, since an error return would invite a discard at each of the 12 call sites |

**Detection is by content, never by filename or config key.** The first
non-blank line's leading `{` decides. This is what keeps `managedBlock()`,
`ProtectedFiles`, `install-hooks` and `chat-history-file` untouched, so existing
users are unaffected — and because there is still exactly one transcript path,
there is still one session directory and one `state.json`, so turn-end dedup
needed no per-format keying. Prefix matching rather than a trial
`json.Unmarshal` is deliberate: it keeps detection working when the *first* line
is itself truncated, which a stricter check would misread as Markdown and turn
into a silently empty session.

**Four things the new format fixes.**

1. **Session identity.** `parseTurnEnd` returns `nil` when the session ID is
   empty, and the Markdown ID is derived from a run banner. JSONL states
   `session_id` outright — but it is sanitised the same way, because it becomes
   a path component. Disallowed characters are *replaced*, not rejected:
   discarding the ID would return `""` and drop the checkpoint, which is the
   exact silent capture loss the structured format was meant to remove.
2. **Token counts are exact.** `input_tokens: 8421`, not Markdown's rounded
   `8.4k`.
3. **`ExtractSummary` finally has something to report.** `checkpoint_created`
   carries the agent's own `summary`, `intent` and `open_questions`. Markdown
   still reports none — that is a property of the format, not of aider, and
   inventing one there would still be a guess.
4. **A real `session_ended` event** exists, where aider previously had none.

**One trade made explicitly.** `ChunkTranscript`'s original comment already
predicted this case: *"a JSONL chunker must reject an oversized line because
splitting a JSON object corrupts it, but Markdown has no such constraint."* The
formats now answer `SplittableMidLine()` differently. Markdown keeps its
byte-level fallback and honours the size budget. JSONL emits an oversized line
whole, as a single over-budget chunk — reassembly is concatenation, so it still
round-trips exactly, and a corrupted JSON object is worse than a chunk over
budget.

**What was deliberately *not* done.** `FormatResumeCommand` still emits
`aider --restore-chat-history`, documented in-source as **unverified** for
JSONL. The flag is confirmed against the Markdown history
(`base_coder.py:520`); whether it also accepts JSONL has not been checked
against aider's source. Emitting an invented flag would fail exactly when the
user needs the resume, and dropping the capability would break every existing
user. No speculative schema was added either: `jsonlEvent` declares only fields
actually observed in the format.

**Verification.** Tests were written to fail first, covering all four required
groups — original Markdown, new JSONL, unknown events, and a truncated final
line at four different cut points. The truncated cases assert the turns parsed
so far, a still-resolvable session ID, and explicitly fail on an empty result.

```
before:  45 top-level tests · 65 cases · 92.1% coverage
after:   71 top-level tests · 108 cases · 93.3% coverage
```

The four original test files are **byte-identical** to the pre-curveball commit
(`git diff --stat` empty), and running exactly the 45 original test names still
yields 65 passing cases. Nothing was rewritten to accommodate the new format.
